q: Under Table VII.1, what is the allowable maximum TGFA for a Basic R-2 inside lot without firewalls?
n: Table VII.1 allows a Basic R-2 inside lot without firewalls a maximum TGFA of 3 storeys × 60% of TLA (PSO). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1.

q: Under Table VII.1, what is the allowable maximum TGFA for a Basic R-2 interior lot without firewalls?
n: Table VII.1 allows a Basic R-2 interior lot without firewalls 3 × 70% of TLA. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1.

q: Under Table VII.1, what is the allowable maximum TGFA for a Basic R-2 corner lot with a firewall?
n: With a firewall, a Basic R-2 corner lot is allowed 3 × 75% of TLA. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1.

q: Under Table VII.1, what is the allowable maximum TGFA for a Basic R-2 through lot without firewalls?
n: Table VII.1 allows a Basic R-2 through lot without firewalls 3 × 70% of TLA. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1.

q: Under Table VII.1, what is the allowable maximum TGFA for a Basic R-2 corner-through lot without firewalls?
n: Table VII.1 allows a Basic R-2 corner-through lot without firewalls 3 × 70% of TLA. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Table VII.1.

q: What minimum fire-resistive rating do Types II and III construction need?
n: Types II and III construction need at least one-hour fire-resistive ratings for their structural elements. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 401; NBC IRR Rule IV.

q: A "traditional indigenous family dwelling" is one of native materials whose total cost does not exceed:
n: A traditional indigenous family dwelling of native materials (bamboo, nipa, logs, lumber) costing at most ₱15,000 is exempt from a building permit. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule II, Sec. 203.

q: What is the riverbank easement in urban areas?
n: The easement along riverbanks in urban areas is 3 m. No buildings may be built within this strip, which stays open for public use, navigation and flood protection. Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51.

q: What is the riverbank easement in agricultural areas?
n: The easement along riverbanks in agricultural areas is 20 m (40 m in forest areas). Source: PD 1067 (Water Code), Art. 51.

q: Dead end length.
n: Dead-end corridors and exterior exit balconies may not exceed 6.00 m in length. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the parking slot size for a jeepney or shuttle?
n: A jeepney or shuttle parking slot is 3.00 × 9.00 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707 (parking slot sizes).

q: What is the parking slot size for a truck or bus?
n: A truck or bus parking slot is 3.60 × 12.00 m. The larger slot fits the length and turning needs of trucks and buses. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.

q: Under Table VIII.4, how many air changes per hour does a restaurant kitchen with a 2.40 m ceiling need?
n: Table VIII.4 gives a restaurant kitchen with a 2.40 m ceiling 5 air changes per hour, dropping to 1½ at 6.10 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Table VIII.4.

q: Under Table VIII.4, how many air changes per hour does an office with a 2.40 m ceiling need?
n: Table VIII.4 gives an office with a 2.40 m ceiling 4 air changes per hour, dropping to 1 at 6.10 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Table VIII.4.

q: Area of view panel:
n: Doors to a smokeproof or exit enclosure may have a view panel of at most 1,300 cm². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the least dimension of a habitable room?
n: A habitable room must have a least dimension of 2.00 m and at least 6.00 m² of floor area. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.

q: What is the minimum area of a kitchen?
n: A kitchen must have at least 3.00 m² of floor area, with a least dimension of 1.50 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.

q: TGFA stands for:
n: TGFA means Total Gross Floor Area: the GFA plus enclosed support areas such as covered parking and service areas. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (definitions).

q: Under the NBC IRR, what is the maximum number of boarders allowed in a boarding house in an R-1 zone?
n: Boarding houses allowed in R-1 zones may have no more than 8 boarders. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 701 (R-1 uses).

q: What is the minimum clear width of a window serving as an emergency exit?
n: A window used as an emergency exit must have a clear opening at least 820 mm wide and 1.00 m high, with its sill no higher than 820 mm. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 808.

q: On how many sides may a firewall be built in an R-2 use?
n: In R-2 use, a firewall may be built on one side only, up to 80% of that side property line. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: What is the BHL if the only road serving the lot is 6 m or 7 m wide?
n: A lot served by a single 6.00–7.00 m RROW is limited to a building height of 3 storeys. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707 (BHL by RROW width).

q: GFA stands for:
n: GFA means Gross Floor Area, the total floor space within the perimeter of the permanent exterior walls. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (definitions).

q: What is the minimum cross-section of a vent shaft per meter of shaft height?
n: A vent shaft needs at least 1.00 m² of cross-section per metre of shaft height, with a least dimension of 600 mm. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 809.

q: How many years of diversified experience does a Building Official need?
n: A Building Official must have at least five years of diversified professional experience in building design and construction. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 206; NBC IRR Rule II.

q: No building may be built unless it adjoins or has direct access to a:
n: No building may be built unless it adjoins or has direct access to a public space (street, alley or public open space). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 803.

q: What is the most vertical distance allowed between stair landings?
n: No stairway may have a vertical rise of more than 3.60 m between landings. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the maximum width of a single exit door leaf?
n: No leaf of an exit door may exceed 1.20 m in width. Limiting leaf width keeps doors light enough to open easily and swing clear during evacuation. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What share of a firewall may be openings?
n: A firewall must be solid and unpierced, with no openings. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: What is the minimum live load of the ground floor of a dwelling?
n: Under the NBC IRR, the first (ground) floor of a dwelling carries a minimum live load of 200 kg/m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 708.

q: What is the minimum live load of the second floor of a dwelling?
n: The second floor of a dwelling carries a minimum live load of 150 kg/m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 708.

q: A change in use is allowed if the new use is ______ in life and fire risk than the existing one.
n: A change in use is allowed if the new use is less hazardous, in life and fire risk, than the existing one. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 104; NBC IRR Rule I.

q: A firewall may run up to 85% of each side property line, two sides, with total firewall length at most 65% of the perimeter. Which use is this?
n: R-3 allows firewalls up to 85% of each side property line on two sides, with total firewall length at most 65% of the perimeter. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: A firewall may run up to 80% of one side property line only. Which use is this?
n: R-2 allows a firewall up to 80% of one side property line only. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: In which residential zone are firewalls not allowed at all?
n: R-1 (low-density residential) does not allow firewalls. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: A firewall may run up to 75% of each side property line, total at most 50% of the perimeter, up to eight storeys. Which use is this?
n: R-5 allows firewalls up to 75% of each side property line, total at most 50% of the perimeter, up to the eighth storey. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: A firewall may run up to 85% of each side property line, total at most 50% of the perimeter, up to three storeys. Which use is this?
n: R-4 allows firewalls up to 85% of each side property line, total at most 50% of the perimeter, up to three storeys. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 704.

q: Which construction type, of masonry, steel and concrete, has a 4-hour fire rating?
n: Type V construction is four-hour fire-resistive throughout, with structural elements of steel, iron, concrete or masonry. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule IV, Sec. 401.

q: What is the total floor space of main and auxiliary buildings, consisting of the GFA plus enclosed support areas such as covered parking and service areas?
n: Total gross floor area is the floor space of main and auxiliary buildings: the GFA plus enclosed support areas such as covered parking and service areas. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (definitions).

q: Electrical installations must conform to the:
n: Electrical installations must conform to the Philippine Electrical Code. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 1101.

q: Mechanical systems must conform to the:
n: Mechanical systems must conform to the Philippine Mechanical Engineering Code. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 1201.

q: Distance of an off-site parking for residential development:
n: Off-site parking for a development must be within 200 m of it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII, Sec. 707.

q: Site (lot) occupancy is measured at ground level and excludes:
n: Site occupancy is measured at ground level and excludes open courts, yards and light wells. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII.

q: What are paved or built open areas, as opposed to softscape, called?
n: Hardscape is paved or built open areas (walks, plazas, driveways), as opposed to planted softscape. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VII (definitions); Ching.

q: Which is NOT a referral code of the National Building Code?
n: The NBC's referral codes include the Electrical, Structural, Plumbing, Mechanical and Fire Codes. The Civil Code is general law, not a referral code. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule I (referral codes).
